Hence, utility companies are seriously considering the massive deployment of communications infrastructure to inject and transport data signal information, over the original 50/60 Hz power lines. This paper depicts the results obtained from a pilot in a suburban area, embracing both medium voltage (MV) and low voltage (LV) infrastructures. A set of practical measurements will be carried out over both the MV and the LV networks, in order to characterize the performance of the TCP/UDP/IP protocol stack.

articleTitle: Analog Front-End ASIC Requirements for a FDM Broadband Powerline System Enabling Co-Existence
publicationTitle: 2007 IEEE International Symposium on Power Line Communications and Its Applications
abstract: This paper presents a feasible set of analog ASIC requirements optimized to achieve co-existence in a broadband power line communications (PLC) system based on frequency division multiplexing (FDM). FDM is the most straightforward way to achieve co-existence between different systems, however, this involves many design challenges at the circuit level. First, a short description will be given of the PLC system, which is under development in the EU funded IST POWERNET project. It will be shown that conventional receiver architectures, typically designed for time division multiple access (TDMA) schemes, are not well suited for FDM systems e.g. due to challenges arising from near/far situations. Solutions to improve the performance will be discussed and simulation results will be presented of the proposed architecture, based on parameters extracted from circuit designs, to show the feasibility of high bit rates in FDM transceivers.

articleTitle: A High-Speed Power-Line Communication System with band-limited OQAM based Multi-Carrier Transmission
publicationTitle: 2007 IEEE International Symposium on Power Line Communications and Its Applications
abstract: As a method to realize a high-speed communication in home network, the power-line communication (PLC) technique is known. A problem of the PLC is that leakage radiation interferes to existing systems. When OFDM is used in PLC system, the leakage radiation is not sufficiently reduced, even if the subcarriers corresponding to frequency-band of the existing system are never used, because the signal is not strictly band-limited. To solve this problem, each subcarrier must be band-limited. In this paper, we apply the OQAM based multi-carrier transmission (OQAM-MCT) to high-speed PLC system, where each subcarrier is individually band-limited. We also propose a pilot-symbol sequence for frequency offset estimation, symbol-timing detection and channel estimation in the OQAM-MCT system. In this method, the pilot signal-sequence consists of the succession of the same data symbol. Computer simulation results show that the OQAM-MCT system achieves both good transmission rate performance and low out-of-band radiation in the PLC channels. It is also shown that the proposed pilot-sequence improves frequency offset estimation, symbol-timing detection and channel estimation performance as compared with the case of using pseudo-noise sequence.

articleTitle: Convolutional Code Search for Good Permutation Trellis Codes using M-ary FSK
publicationTitle: 2007 IEEE International Symposium on Power Line Communications and Its Applications
abstract: Permutation trellis codes combined with M-ary FSK are considered with the aim of combating additive noise, impulse noise and permanent frequency disturbances. New permutation trellis codes are presented that were found by exhaustive computer search, considering the free distance and the distance spectrum of the codes. Until now the best binary convolutional codes were considered to be the best candidates to use in mappings for trellis codes, however the results will show that this is not always the case. Simulation results are also presented, showing that in most cases the new permutation trellis codes are performing better than the previous codes, although the gains attained are small.

articleTitle: Opera 2: standardization of broadband PLC
publicationTitle: 2007 IEEE International Symposium on Power Line Communications and Its Applications
abstract: The research, technological development and innovation activities of Opera 2 are very related to the standardization of the new generation of PLC integrated network. During OPERA phase 1 a comprehensive specification of the PLC components, that need to be standardized for guaranteeing the interoperability of devices from different manufacturers, was delivered. The OPERA specification version 1 covers both PHY and MAC layers (part 1 of the specification), as well as higher layers' components (part 2 of the specification). OPERA phase 1 also delivered a proposal for an access / in-home coexistence mechanism. During OPERA phase 2, we will issue a second version of the OPERA specification that will be compatible with the future (still to be agreed) access / in-home coexistence standard, and that could / will be recognized as European / worldwide access PLC standard.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Monitoring Software for Heterogeneous Control Network
publicationTitle: 2007 IEEE International Symposium on Power Line Communications and Its Applications
abstract: XCP (extended control protocol) is an information oriented protocol which delivers information with high reliability according to the predefined rule. XCP network system can be implemented on top of several physical layer such as power line, IEEE 802.15.4 and so on. In this paper, a monitoring software that evaluates the reliability and performance of the XCP network is designed and implemented. This paper presents the structure and method of the packet monitoring in the network through several interfaces such as RS-232, ethernet. The feasibility of the implemented software is verified through the experimental evaluation.

articleTitle: Keynote II. Power line channels: frequency and time selective Part 1.-Response of indoor PLC channels
publicationTitle: 2007 IEEE International Symposium on Power Line Communications and Its Applications
abstract: This Keynote discusses the behavior of indoor power line communications (PLC) channels when used for broadband transmission. The focus is put on the channel response characteristics and, particularly, on its time variant character. In order to create a model for a certain communication channel two strategies can be adopted. The first one is to define a structural model, based on the knowledge of the physical properties of the medium. In our case, they are: the power grid layout, the kind of wires installed, the devices connected to them and the points where transmitter and receiver are placed. From this point, a behavioral model can be derived, by calculating the transmission line parameters of the different sections of wire, the transmission matrices and, finally, the channel frequency response. That is a bottom-up approach, increasing the level of abstraction. The second one is to define directly a behavioral model, which is a simplified representation of the expected channel in a statistical sense. It should be based on some prior knowledge of the medium nature to adopt a clever mathematical model. Then, an extensive measurement campaign has to be carried out on different scenarios to adjust the statistical parameters of the model. That is to follow a top-down approach. The second kind of modeling is traditional in wireless channels. For instance, in GSM an impulse response with few echoes is assumed, and the statistical parameters are selected according to the scenario.

articleTitle: Lunch Speech II. HomePlug Standards for Worldwide Multimedia In-Home Networking and Broadband Powerline Access
publicationTitle: 2007 IEEE International Symposium on Power Line Communications and Its Applications
abstract: In 2001, the HomePlug Powerline Alliance released the first International high speed powerline communications standard called HomePlug 1.0.1, which operated at a PHY rate of 14 Mbps. Since that time, more than 7 Million HomePlug 1.0 chips have been sold. An updated product based on HomePlug1.0, called HomePlug 1.0 Turbo and operating at 85Mbps was released in 2004. The most recent HomePlug standard is embodied in the HomePlug AV 1.0 specification, and products complying with this specification and operating at 200 Mbps began to appear in 2006. In addition, the HomePlug Alliance and its members, including Intellon Corporation, are actively engaged in the development of HomePlug BPL and HomePlug Command and Control specifications and products. This presentation will first provide an overview of the HomePlug suite of standards including ongoing work towards BPL and Command and Control specifications as well as an overview of HomePlug1.0. The presentation will then focus on HomePlug AV and will describe in detail the HomePlug AV PHY, MAC and Convergence Layers as well as well as the HomePlug AV certification process. The talk will highlight the key technical advantages of the HomePlug AV when compared with other PLC solutions seeking to satisfy the demand for the high data rates and quality of service requirements for distribution of multimedia throughout the home.

articleTitle: Cross-Layer Designs of Multicarrier NC-PRMA Systems over Powerlines
publicationTitle: 2007 IEEE International Symposium on Power Line Communications and Its Applications
abstract: We study the performance of non-collision packet reservation multiple access (NC-PRMA) scheme as a MAC protocol for powerline communication networks. A PHY-MAC cross layer design is considered in order to provide quality of service (QoS) guarantees for integrated voice, data and video services. System performance is evaluated via simulations in terms of packet dropping probability and mean access delay.

articleTitle: Wide Band, Accurate Estimation for the Primary Parameters of the NA2XCWY Underground Cable
publicationTitle: 2007 IEEE International Symposium on Power Line Communications and Its Applications
abstract: This paper uses the finite element method for the estimation of the primary parameters of an underground, low voltage, power distribution cable. The analysis is performed in view of communication and electromagnetic compatibility issues. Calculations are performed up to 40 MHz, on the basis of an accurate diffusion equation. Comparisons with a specific set of earlier results, which neglect the displacement current, are carried out up to 500 MHz. This cable is widely used by the Hellenic Electric Power Company in urban networks all over Greece. According to the VDE standardization, its code is NA2XCWY.

articleTitle: Experimental field trials of a utility AMR power line communication system analyzing channel effects and error correction methods
publicationTitle: 2007 IEEE International Symposium on Power Line Communications and Its Applications
abstract: This paper analyses the effects of noise in a real automated meter reading (AMR) environment where power line communication (PLC) is used for meter reading. The aim is to give an analysis of periodic noise properties through its effect on a B-FSK based PLC system and to compare different error correction techniques under different constraints of attenuation and noise produced by the real loads installed in the network. Tests have been carried out using two different channel frequencies in the CENELEC A band taking into account frequency dependence of the line.

articleTitle: Low Complexity Turbo Equalisation for Power Line Communications
publicationTitle: 2007 IEEE International Symposium on Power Line Communications and Its Applications
abstract: Due to the highly dispersive nature of the power line channel, there has been a strong trend towards the use of orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) modulation for wideband power line communications (PLC). However, OFDM modulation has the drawbacks of high peak-to-average power ratio and increased sensitivity to carrier synchronisation errors. On the other hand, single-carrier (SC) modulation techniques do not suffer from these problems and they are widely used in low-rate narrowband PLC. For broadband PLC, however, the strong intersymbol interference (ISI) introduced by the power line channel calls for the use of powerful coding and equalisation techniques, such as turbo coding/equalisation. In this paper, we investigate the performance of the so-called soft interference cancellers (SIC) techniques for turbo equalisation (TE) in PLC applications. The results of simulations over powerline channels with different amounts of memory show that, after performing some number of iterations, the SIC-based TE scheme outperforms a COFDM system that uses the same turbo code, over the entire range of SNR values.

articleTitle: A Low Complexity Multicarrier Proposal for Medium Rate Demanding Automatic Meter Reading Systems
publicationTitle: 2007 IEEE International Symposium on Power Line Communications and Its Applications
abstract: In automatic meter reading (AMR) technology, electrical utilities (EUs) have been exploiting their own infrastructure to bill their customers in an efficient and economical way using power line communications (PLC) technologies. Since the amount of data that has to be send is quite low related to the available time to perform this task, AMR applications have been demanding low bit rates. At this moment, EUs are exploring and demanding other services as load and alarm management, remote monitoring and disconnections, etc. In this context, the low voltage PLC modems should provide more throughput while keeping the cost of the hardware low. In this paper, a low complexity multicarrier modulation is proposed in order to exploit the CENELEC A band.

articleTitle: The assessment and Measurement of the signal Regression of Broadband Power Signals in the frequency range 1.6MHz to 30MHz over the low voltage distribution Network
publicationTitle: 2007 IEEE International Symposium on Power Line Communications and Its Applications
abstract: The distribution network that carries the energy for all homes and buildings is providing keen competition to more established communications services such as cable networks and distribution line services including ADSL and VDSL. However the increase of BPL services over the low voltage distribution network leads to potential for radio interference in the short wave band. This consequently has effects on established radio services such as emergency services and military communications. The key electromagnetic compatibility parameter that provides an indicative assessment of interference amongst a series of parameters is the regression rate of the signal radiated from the power cable and will potentially provide an insight into interference modes. The detailed experimental programme will cover the experimental methodology together with the results will be presented and compared with established standards on regression of signals in this frequency band.

articleTitle: HV-DPLC SELTA experience and standard needs vision
publicationTitle: 2007 IEEE International Symposium on Power Line Communications and Its Applications
abstract: After 30 years of activity in designing and producing Power Line Carrier systems for the HV power lines, SELTA approached the brand new Digital PLC technology eight years ago. SELTA developed a family of equipment based on 64 Trellis Code Modulation. These equipment also integrate an Echo Canceller with the goal to improve the spectral efficiency. SELTA strongly supports any modification of the International Norm IEC495 (or eventually a new International Norm) concerning the Analogue PLC technology in order to fit it to the Digital ones. It is worth to underline that the new Digital equipment are fully compatible with the Analogue ones, so to assure a reasonable substitution in the next years. The digital links, thus granting a very low level of BER (10E-6), must also supply an high availability. To reach this result some critical events on the carriers must be considered, such as: noise, spikes, frequency interferences, circuit breaker operations strongly changing signal level and impedance.

publicationTitle: 2007 IEEE International Symposium on Power Line Communications and Its Applications
abstract: Communications Services provision in developing countries pose some challenges. Technologies available such as GSM, GSM/GPRS, WCDMA, CDMA2000,WLL,ADSL etc VSAT/Satellite can provide services in different remote areas and municipality. Although above mentioned technologies already implemented still data accessibility in some rural/municipality and low populated is a problem. Due to the Proposal of UN-ICT task force, ICT can be used for Poverty reductions in most of developing Countries. This can be realized by accessing data (internet & Associated Services). In order to be able to access Internet and other services e.g. e-Learning, e-Health, e-Government, e-Commerce we need different initiatives.

articleTitle: Systematic analysis of electromagnetic emissions and susceptibility in BPL system
publicationTitle: 2007 IEEE International Symposium on Power Line Communications and Its Applications
abstract: Aim of this paper is to carry on a systematic analysis of the unwanted electromagnetic emissions of a typical span of an overhead three phase power line when operated by a broadband communication power line (BPL) system. This is done by considering different scenarios of the presence of the ground plane and of the metallic poles (or towers) at the end of the span. The used numerical technique, the method of moments, allows one to evaluate also the induced voltages at the termination of the line when an external electromagnetic wave impinges the line. This allows the evaluation of the induced noise voltage.

articleTitle: High-voltage PLC roles in packet-switching networks of power utilities
publicationTitle: 2007 IEEE International Symposium on Power Line Communications and Its Applications
abstract: High-voltage PLC communications need redefinition of its roles in packet-switching networks of power utilities. The paper presents a classification of data and services of the power system communications and proposes some adjustments in the TCP/IP reference model to ensure reliable incorporation of PLC links in the packet-oriented power-utility communication systems. A brief description of high-voltage PLC systems is given with emphasis on their role in current power utility communications. The research needs to answer how TCP operates in the network containing PLC links.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of CSK/PAM System Using Optimized Real-Valued Sequence
publicationTitle: 2007 IEEE International Symposium on Power Line Communications and Its Applications
abstract: We propose applying pulse amplitude modulated code shift keying (CSK/PAM) to indoor power line communication (PLC) for the high-speed data transmission at the low electromagnetic wave leakage. However, CSK/PAM system using conventional binary sequence, for example Gold sequence and M sequence, has error floor for real power line channels even with rake receiver because of the poor properties of odd auto-and cross-correlation. Therefore, we propose extending binary sequence to real-valued sequence and we optimize performance in real-valued sequence by minimizing the even and odd, auto-and cross-correlation values. We show that the CSK/PAM system using the optimized real-valued sequence can achieve better BER (bit error rate) performance as compared with that using Gold sequence by computer simulation.

articleTitle: Digital PLC technology to support the MV and HV grid remote control: practical experience and standardisation open issues
publicationTitle: 2007 IEEE International Symposium on Power Line Communications and Its Applications
abstract: MV and LV distribution networks are evolving from purely passive towards active grids with generation units directly connected. This comes from the technical evolution of small generation units but, mainly, is driven by electric energy market liberalisation that is bringing new actors to share and contribute to the same infrastructure. The above scenario asks for a new control system, that must be sound from the technical viewpoint to ensure the power quality, and a monitoring and metering system at the interfaces between the different actors. The control system will be based on distributed objects, with a high degree of autonomy, but needs a coordination level. Power line technology is the natural candidate to implement the communication infrastructure to support the control system. Main characteristics of the communication system are summarised along with up to date technical solutions and main open issues.

articleTitle: A Fuzzy-Logic model for impulsive noise in PLC
publicationTitle: 2007 IEEE International Symposium on Power Line Communications and Its Applications
abstract: In this paper an unsupervised classification procedure is proposed for the identification of different types of impulsive noise affecting an outdoor high voltage power line channel. Clustering of the time domain recorded data is preformed by a feature-based approach. Principal component analysis (PCA) is performed on the normalized spectra and clustering is performed on the principal components using a subtractive clustering method and fuzzy c-means (FCM). Several types of disturbances are recognized, arriving from different kinds of excitation. Finally coloring AR filters are designed for modeling each kind of noise. The proposed procedure has been applied to experimentally recorded noise data.

abstract: This paper presents a model proposed by GITUN Group (Telecommunications Research Group of the National University of Colombia) about using Colombian low voltage distribution lines as data transmission channel for Automatic Meter Reading (AMR) applications. Residential energy electromechanical meter, reading and transmission data are studied, also electrical noise measurement and simulations are developed for Colombian low voltage distribution lines (117VAC Phase-Neutral 60Hz) which affects data transmission using PLC in AMR. Laboratory essays and one real essays over one energized power network with real user connected permit to find the communications channel model and noise effects, which is simulated using MATLAB and ATP to determine technical possibility of the use of AMR system via PLC in Colombia, and both compared. Finally, involved PLC regulations in Colombia are shown as the same as technical and economical benefits.

articleTitle: Mathematical Modeling of Conducted EMI in an Independent Power Supply System Including Power Line Communication Technology
publicationTitle: 2007 IEEE International Symposium on Power Line Communications and Its Applications
abstract: The paper presents a way of solving the electromagnetic interference (EMI) problem for an electric power system with power line communication, supplied from an autonomous power source. Theoretical results include a mathematical model of the system with power line communication derived from the recently introduced multi-phase bridge-element concept. Numerical experiments are performed in two steps. Firstly, a mathematical model of the electric power system is developed and realized in software for the system including a three-phase synchronous generator, a switch-mode power supply with an equivalent load, a source and a single-frequency power line modem represented by the circuit extracting the data signal. Secondly, an AC/DC/AC converter with an integrated active filter is included in the model. Current waveforms and spectra of data signal are compared at the modem input. Numerical experiments demonstrate applicability of the developed mathematical models in the power line communication design and the efficiency of the proposed way of integrating the power line communication technology into the power system including the sources of conducted emissions.

articleTitle: Notch Elimination by Halfway Termination of Powerline and Matched Coupling Method
publicationTitle: 2007 IEEE International Symposium on Power Line Communications and Its Applications
abstract: On the powerline communication method, there is a problem of the notch frequencies of the powerline. The notch frequency is a frequency with very low impedance. It is generated by a reflection at the end of powerline. Data transmission is obstacle at the notch frequencies. Notch frequencies are unpredictable because they depend on the length of powerline and the length of powerline varies with user's circumstance. In the preceding technology, this problem was avoided with putting a matched terminator at the end of the powerline or using matched adaptive filter to avoid communication at notch frequencies. However, the terminator is not easily set up because it is difficult to find the end of the powerline in the practical situations. Matched filter needs high computational effort to find the optimum filter parameters. In this paper, it is presented that an improvement of frequency characteristics was observed in an experiment when the terminator was put on the halfway of the powerline. Further, a matched coupling circuit is proposed which enables communication through powerline between the two terminators put on the halfway of a powerline. In this method, terminators can be put on any places where two terminators sandwich communication sites. Hence, it would be much more applicable to most of practical situations where powerlines are covered by wall.

articleTitle: CATP: Collective Acknowledgement Transmission Protocol for Group Commands in PLC Networks based on the SFN Technique
publicationTitle: 2007 IEEE International Symposium on Power Line Communications and Its Applications
abstract: The problem of covering large Powerline Communications (PLC) networks can be solved by the application of the Single Frequency Network (SFN) technique, building so-called PLC-SFN systems. Such networks are used for various control systems which require confirmations of transmitted commands. This is realized by an acknowledgement transmitted from the slave stations to a master. However, in the considered PLC-SFN systems, applied for ground traffic control in airports with very strong requirements, it is necessary to ensure a reliable acknowledgement transmission within reasonable time boundaries according to the considered application. The both requirements can be ensured by the so-called Collective Acknowledgement Transmission Protocol (CATP), presented in this paper. The CATP is based on a two-phase reservation method for the acknowledgement transmission with the help of so-called collective stations, which are chosen in accordance with specific algorithms. The algorithms are also presented.

articleTitle: Lunch Speech I. Broadband Powerline for Power Distribution Applications
publicationTitle: 2007 IEEE International Symposium on Power Line Communications and Its Applications
abstract: European Power Utilities are facing huge changes these days. The liberalization of the energy market leads to decreased margins as well as national regulatory bodies' demand for higher transparency. Utilities are in need to gather more information about the actual status and load of their electricity grid. Information, is only decentralized available on different sites within the whole power grid. A lot of different communication technologies are used today to collect all the demanded data, e.g. Narrowband PLC or GSM for automatic meter reading, copper twisted pair for the control of RTU (Remote Terminal Units) or fibre optical networks for SCADA (Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition) systems. For each of these applications a new communication network has to be build up and operated. With Broadband Powerline Communication Systems (PLC) utilities could set up one communication platform for the data transportation of all the applications mentioned above. The PLC Technology enables various IP-based services by broadband data transfer from and to every point of the electric network. And this technology enables utilities to use their own infrastructure, the distribution network, as a communication network. This Keynote will present implementation and migration strategies for power utilities to IP based Broadband Powerline Communications Systems. It will show the aspects on a technical and user requirement based approach for enhanced utility communication. Intelligent network and grid communication for industrial and household application will be depicted with respect to existing communication media and applications.

articleTitle: High-Quality Video Distribution using Power Line Communication and Aplication Layer Forward Error Correction
publicationTitle: 2007 IEEE International Symposium on Power Line Communications and Its Applications
abstract: Power line communications (PLC) has proven its merits an in-house broadband communication network for IP services. However, designing challenging applications on such networks is still difficult task because of the "horrible channel". Long bursts of errors often occur as a result of e.g. cross-talk, radio-frequency interference and impulse noise making reliable communication quite difficult. Local means for QoS provision such as retransmission protocols have been studied. However, often in-house link is only the last hop in an end-to-end service with specific QoS requirements. For example, for high-quality video distribution in an end-to-end IPTV services, reliability, real-time, and low latency are essential. IPTV services nowadays already make use of application layer forward error correction codes to compensate longer outages of several milliseconds. Therefore, the inclusion of the in-house power line network into this end-to-end QoS architecture seems natural and straightforward. A prominent example of such FEC codes is the Raptor code which has recently been adopted for application layer FEC for DVB IPTV services. In this work, we study the application of Raptor codes for IPTV services and show that typical experienced long outages can be compensated by these codes. The results are complemented by interesting findings in system design which might lead to future optimizations of power line communications.

articleTitle: Fast Burst Synchronization for PLC Systems
publicationTitle: 2007 IEEE International Symposium on Power Line Communications and Its Applications
abstract: Fast burst synchronization is an important requirement in various power line communication (PLC) networks, where devices transmit short data packets in an unscheduled fashion. Such a synchronization is typically achieved by means of a preamble sent in front of the data packet. In this paper, we discuss the appropriate receiver processing of the preamble signal and devise a new preamble-design approach, which takes the most distinctive characteristics of the power line channel and important practical constraints into account. A comprehensive performance study shows that an exemplary designed preamble consistently outperforms conventional preamble sequences.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Channel Allocation Problem in Broadband Power Line Communications Access Networks
publicationTitle: 2007 IEEE International Symposium on Power Line Communications and Its Applications
abstract: The planning process of the broadband powerline communications access network is composed of two problems; the generalized base station placement problem and the PLC channel allocation problem. In this paper, we investigate the PLC channel allocation problem and formulate it as a multi-objective combinatorial optimization (MOO) problem. Its objectives are mathematically formulated with the boundary limits that constrain their optimization. Metaheuristics based on evolutionary search are used to solve it. Two approaches are applied for this optimization: a classical approach that converts the MOO problem into a single-objective optimization (SOO) problem; and a more recent approach based on the multi-objective optimization algorithms. The performances of SOO and MOO are evaluated by numerical experiments.

articleTitle: Joint Decoding of TCM and Detection of PTS Side Information: a Multiple Trellis Solution
publicationTitle: 2007 IEEE International Symposium on Power Line Communications and Its Applications
abstract: One of the major drawback of orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) systems is the large Peak-to-Average power Ratio (PAR) of the transmit signal. High levels of PAR may be a limiting factor for power line communication (PLC) where regulatory bodies have fixed the maximum amount of transmit power. Partial transmit sequence (PTS) is a well-known solution for PAR reduction, but its effectiveness depends on an accurate, and possibly error-free, exchange of side information (SI) between the transmitter and the receiver. In this article, a new maximum likelihood (ML) algorithm for joint decoding of trellis code modulation (TCM) and detection of PTS is presented. The proposed algorithm exploits the redundancy introduced by the TCM code to estimate the correct PTS, and represents a practical solution to avoid the explicit insertion of SI into the OFDM signal. The proposed algorithm has been assessed by bit-error rate (BER) simulation, showing a good performance over additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) channels and amplifier nonlinearities.

Author Keywords: joint maximum likelihood sequence detection and decoding

articleTitle: Lessons Learned from Wireless Sensor Networks with Application to AMR and PLC
publicationTitle: 2007 IEEE International Symposium on Power Line Communications and Its Applications
abstract: Automatic meter reading (AMR) presents many parallelisms with the fast emerging field of wireless sensor networks (WSN) even if for this purpose they use the power cables as transmission medium. Among these parallelisms it is worthwhile to mention that both systems are essentially multihop and operate in a very noisy environment. For this reason the present paper reviews relevant results in the field of WSN with application to PLC based AMR systems and extracts lessons applicable to AMR and to PLC in general. Based on these lessons, this paper develops a theoretical model called the "star of chains model" with regularly spaced devices forming chains that connect to a concentrator station, which is useful to derive the capacity of a system and to provide some basic rules of the thumb for creating it. A specific and simple MAC layer protocol based on the WSN protocol known as "ripple control" is proposed to take the most out of the presented model. This protocol allows for good throughput while coping with the necessary retransmissions in noisy environments and with the necessary creation of periods of contention for the automatic registration of new nodes. The protocol may useful also for other applications in narrow band PLC as well as in broadband powerline communications (BPL). A simulation based on OPNET modeler has been developed to check the capacity calculations. The model and protocol presented are a first step that will be refined and extended in the future.

articleTitle: Turbo-Fuzzy Equalization for Single-Carrier Power Line Channels
publicationTitle: 2007 IEEE International Symposium on Power Line Communications and Its Applications
abstract: This paper introduces a turbo-fuzzy equalizer (TFEQ) to cope with the inter-symbol interference effects and impulsive noise occurrences in bandlimited digital communication channels, such as the indoor and outdoor power line circuits. We exploit a close relationship between the fuzzy and Bayesian equalizers to derive an adaptive nonsingleton turbo-fuzzy equalization technique. Generally speaking, the TFEQ is obtained by introducing an adaptive decision feedback nonsingleton fuzzy equalizer into the turbo equalization structure. Simulation results reveal the applicability of this approach to overcome the noise impairments in the power line frequency range for broadband applications.

articleTitle: Robust Detection in Power Line Communication for OFDM and non-Rayleigh Fading Channels
publicationTitle: 2007 IEEE International Symposium on Power Line Communications and Its Applications
abstract: This paper presents a receiver implementation that uses robust detection and estimation techniques on top of Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing to eliminate various forms of interference associated with the powerline communication channel, namely, non-Rayleigh fading and highly impulsive noise. Computation of error probabilities and Relative Efficiencies with respect to the locally most powerful, maximum likelihood, and optimum parametric detectors demonstrates that the proposed techniques maintain a nearly optimum performance for small signal to noise ratios regardless of the degree of noise contamination and interference. Moreover, the theory of proposed techniques can be easily extended to include operation in a multiuser multiple access network environment.

articleTitle: Bit-Transport Capability of Broadband Multicarrier Power Line Channels Constrained by Radiated Emission
publicationTitle: 2007 IEEE International Symposium on Power Line Communications and Its Applications
abstract: A procedure is proposed to test the bit-transport capability of the multi-carrier scheme on distribution power networks in the frequency range of 1-30 MHz. A frequency-dependent rigorous model of medium-voltage power networks made of branches of three-phase lines above a dissipative ground is utilized. The radiated electromagnetic field is predicted by means of a full wave procedure in the high frequency range taking into account the ground propagation. The integer-bit loading procedure presents as a target the optimal bit-allocation in the sub-channels having the same bandwidth and the maximization of the total bit-rate. The constraints imposed by the source are the power level and the radiated electromagnetic field. Networking aspects are considered both for the effect of crosstalk induced by the presence of multiple users/stations and for policies accounting for the QoS requests coming from the users. Different policies are investigated by considering both fairness requirements, that reduce the network net rate, and unfair approach able to maximize the network rate without considering "all" the QoS requirements. The procedure is applied for the optimal bits allocation on the sub-channels of a medium voltage power network with a tree-type configuration made by five branches.

articleTitle: Aerial MV lines at VHF/UHF: A Versatile Broadband Hybrid Wireless/Wireline Channel
publicationTitle: 2007 IEEE International Symposium on Power Line Communications and Its Applications
abstract: Initial channel modeling and simulation of the Medium Voltage (MV) power lines (11 - 66 KV) in India have indicated very high bandwidths, comparable to Metro fiber. This paper further elucidates this communication channel. We discuss its static variations and its (fading) dynamics. We show how a wide variety of wireline offerings are available - Gigabit scale backbone through broadband access, at a variety of repeater spacings. In addition, we show a unique characteristic of the MV powerline at VHF/UHF, it both radiates as well as transmits - resulting in a hybrid wireless-wireline channel, serving both high speed broadband as well as ubiquitous mobility applications, including 3G/4G. Our results show that rates close to the Shannon bound can be achieved in these applications, using classical transceiver techniques.

articleTitle: Effect of Narrow Band Disturbances over Power Line Channels Using Multicarrier Modulation
publicationTitle: 2007 IEEE International Symposium on Power Line Communications and Its Applications
abstract: Orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) is used for broadband communications over power line due to its ability to adapt to complex transmission channel structures. OFDM is a multicarrier modulation system based on the discrete Fourier transform. However, its poor spectral containment decreases the system performance in front of narrow-band interferences. In order to improve the performance of the communication system, general MCM systems are implemented using filter bank transformations. Both perfect reconstruction and near perfect reconstruction filter banks are considered. It is shown that near perfect reconstruction filter banks achieve the lowest probability of error. Lately, in order to implement these techniques to frequency selective channels, a set of equalization techniques are presented and their performances are evaluated.

articleTitle: Standardization issues of Digital Power Line Communication over high voltage lines
publicationTitle: 2007 IEEE International Symposium on Power Line Communications and Its Applications
abstract: Due to the present lack of a product standard for Digital PLC terminals communicating over high voltage power lines, the question arises how the existing standard IEC60495 "Single sideband power line carrier terminals" should be interpreted suitably for digital and mixed analog/digital PLC terminals such that coexistence with analog and digital PLC terminals on the same power lines is possible. The question had to be answered for the specification of ABBs new power line terminal ETL600 that can be configured for pure digital, pure analog or mixed analog/digital operation. The presentation shows how this has been done, points out open standardization problems and makes propositions for solving them.
